name: Basic Java
description: A structured learning dataset covering the fundamentals of Java programming for beginners.

Introduction to Java.explanation: Java is a high-level, object-oriented, class-based programming language designed to be platform-independent. Java programs are compiled into bytecode that runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM).
key_points: Java is platform-independent because of the JVM.
Java source files normally use the .java extension.
Java programs are compiled into bytecode.
The Java compiler is called javac.
The Java Virtual Machine executes Java bytecode.

JDK, JRE and JVM.explanation: JDK, JRE, and JVM are important components of the Java platform. The JDK is used to develop Java applications, the JRE provides the environment needed to run Java applications, and the JVM executes Java bytecode.
key_points: JDK stands for Java Development Kit.
JRE stands for Java Runtime Environment.
JVM stands for Java Virtual Machine.
JDK contains development tools such as javac.
JRE provides libraries and the JVM needed to run applications.

Java Program Structure.explanation: A basic Java program contains a class and usually a main method. Program execution begins from the main method when the class is run.
points_to_remember: The main method is the entry point of a standard Java application.
Statements normally end with a semicolon.
Curly braces define blocks of code.

Comments.explanation: Comments are notes written inside source code. They are ignored by the Java compiler and are useful for explaining code.

Variables.explanation: A variable is a named memory location used to store a value. Every variable has a data type and a name.
points_to_remember: Variables must have a declared type.
A variable can be reassigned unless declared final.
Local variables must be initialized before use.

Constants.explanation: A constant is a variable whose value cannot be changed after initialization. The final keyword is used to create constants.
Constants.code:
final double PI = 3.14159;
final int MAX_USERS = 100;
points_to_remember: Constants are commonly written using uppercase letters.
A final variable can be initialized only once.

Primitive Data Types.explanation: Java has eight primitive data types used to store simple values directly.

Non-Primitive Data Types.explanation: Non-primitive types store references to objects rather than simple primitive values.

Type Casting.explanation: Type casting converts a value from one data type to another. Widening conversion happens automatically when converting a smaller compatible numeric type to a larger one. Narrowing conversion requires explicit casting.

Arithmetic Operators.explanation: Arithmetic operators are used to perform mathematical calculations.

Assignment Operators.explanation: Assignment operators assign values to variables and can combine assignment with arithmetic operations.

Relational Operators.explanation: Relational operators compare two values and return a boolean result.

Ternary Operator.explanation: The ternary operator is a short form of an if-else expression.

String Concatenation.explanation: The + operator can be used to combine strings and other values.

Input using Scanner.explanation: The Scanner class can be used to read input from the keyboard.

If Statement.explanation: The if statement executes a block of code when a condition evaluates to true.

If Else Statement.explanation: The if-else statement chooses between two blocks of code based on a condition.

Else If Ladder.explanation: An else-if ladder checks multiple conditions in sequence.

Switch Statement.explanation: The switch statement selects one block of code based on the value of an expression.

For Loop.explanation: A for loop repeats a block of code when the number of iterations is known or controlled by a loop condition.

While Loop.explanation: A while loop repeatedly executes code while its condition remains true.

Do While Loop.explanation: A do-while loop executes its body at least once before checking the condition.

Break Statement.explanation: The break statement immediately terminates the nearest loop or switch statement.

Continue Statement.explanation: The continue statement skips the current iteration and moves to the next iteration of a loop.

Methods.explanation: A method is a reusable block of code designed to perform a specific task.

Method Overloading.explanation: Method overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists.

Arrays.explanation: An array stores multiple values of the same type in a fixed-size structure.
important_points: All elements normally have the same data type.
The length property gives the number of elements.

Array Traversal.explanation: Array elements can be accessed using traditional loops or enhanced for loops.

Two Dimensional Arrays.explanation: A two-dimensional array can represent data in rows and columns.

String Basics.explanation: String represents a sequence of characters. Strings are objects in Java and are immutable.

Object Oriented Programming.explanation: Object-oriented programming organizes software around objects and classes. Java supports major OOP concepts including encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

Class.explanation: A class is a blueprint for creating objects. It defines fields and methods that objects created from the class can have.

Object.explanation: An object is an instance of a class. Objects contain state through fields and behavior through methods.

Constructor.explanation: A constructor is a special member used to initialize objects. It has the same name as the class and does not have a return type.

this Keyword.explanation: The this keyword refers to the current object.

Encapsulation.explanation: Encapsulation means restricting direct access to an object's internal state and providing controlled access through methods.

Inheritance.explanation: Inheritance allows one class to acquire fields and methods from another class.

Method Overriding.explanation: Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides its own implementation of a method inherited from its parent class.

Polymorphism.explanation: Polymorphism allows the same interface or method call to represent different behaviors. Compile-time polymorphism is commonly achieved through overloading, while runtime polymorphism is commonly achieved through overriding.

Abstraction.explanation: Abstraction hides implementation details and exposes only the essential behavior. Java supports abstraction using abstract classes and interfaces.

Interfaces.explanation: An interface defines a contract that implementing classes can follow. Interfaces are commonly used to achieve abstraction and support multiple inheritance of type.

Access Modifiers.explanation: Access modifiers control the visibility of classes, fields, constructors, and methods.

modifiers.public: Accessible from anywhere subject to normal Java access rules.
modifiers.private: Accessible only within the declaring class.
modifiers.protected: Accessible within the same package and in subclasses under Java's protected-access rules.
modifiers.default: When no modifier is specified, access is limited to the same package.

static Keyword.explanation: The static keyword indicates that a field or method belongs to the class rather than to individual objects.

final Keyword.explanation: The final keyword can prevent reassignment of variables, overriding of methods, or inheritance of classes.

Wrapper Classes.explanation: Wrapper classes provide object representations of primitive values.

Autoboxing and Unboxing.explanation: Autoboxing automatically converts a primitive value into its corresponding wrapper object. Unboxing converts a wrapper object back into a primitive.

Exception Handling.explanation: Exception handling allows a program to handle abnormal situations without unnecessarily terminating program execution.

Packages.explanation: Packages organize related Java classes and help avoid naming conflicts.

Import Statement.explanation: The import statement allows classes from other packages to be used without writing their fully qualified names.

Garbage Collection.explanation: Java automatically manages memory and can reclaim memory occupied by objects that are no longer reachable.
points_to_remember: System.gc() only requests garbage collection; it does not guarantee immediate collection.
Modern Java code should not rely on finalization.

Command Line Arguments.explanation: Command-line arguments are values passed to a Java program when it is started. They are available through the String[] args parameter of main.

Enums.explanation: An enum defines a fixed set of named constants.

Basic Java Best Practices.explanation: Following basic coding practices makes Java programs easier to read, maintain, and debug.
points: Use meaningful variable and method names.
Keep methods focused on a single responsibility.
Use comments when they clarify non-obvious logic.
Prefer readable code over unnecessarily clever code.
Use constants for values that should not change.
Close resources appropriately or use try-with-resources.

Basic Java Practice Problems.explanation: These problems help beginners practice the fundamentals of Java.
problems: Print Hello World.
Add two numbers.
Find the largest of two numbers.
Find the largest of three numbers.
Check whether a number is even or odd.
Check whether a number is positive, negative, or zero.
Calculate the factorial of a number.
Print a multiplication table.
Reverse a number.
Check whether a number is a palindrome.
Check whether a number is prime.
Print prime numbers within a range.
Calculate the sum of array elements.
Find the maximum element in an array.
Find the minimum element in an array.
Search for an element in an array.
Reverse an array.
Count vowels in a string.
Reverse a string.
Check whether a string is a palindrome.
Create a Student class.
Create a BankAccount class using encapsulation.
Demonstrate inheritance using Animal and Dog classes.
Demonstrate method overloading.
Demonstrate method overriding.
Handle division by zero using exception handling.
